page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Cache resources include a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU score placing in the top 25%. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile operations, which contributes to top-tier performance in image processing and static web serving throughput. Memory performance is robust, with read-only cached memory bandwidth reaching 5112.66 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 197.6 GB/sec. Large-block write bandwidth and single-core stress-ng performance sit in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i-flex.16xlarge leverages high-density DDR5 memory and dedicated CPU allocation to deliver strong compute-per-resource value without the premium of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions allows it to handle specialized workloads like LLM inference on medium and large models efficiently on CPU. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing.
